query: High-entropy alloys can combine mechanical strength, wear resistance, corrosion protection, oxidation resistance, and thermal stability, while their large compositional space offers opportunities to tune degradation in harsh environments. Prior studies have largely considered wear and corrosion separately, and only a few reports address their combined action, leaving the governing behavior poorly understood. For a high-entropy alloy subjected to tribo-corrosion, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the coupled response and why? Describe a controlled comparison that would isolate the governing cause, predict changes in total degradation and its wear and corrosion components relative to a matched baseline, state where the prediction should hold or fail, connect it to the available prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In aqueous tribo-corrosion of face-centred-cubic Cr-containing high-entropy alloys, the coupled (synergy) component of material loss is governed mainly by the ability of the alloy to form and retain a nanocrystalline, Cr/Mn-rich spinel tribo-oxide film whose growth is slowed by sluggish cation diffusion. Increasing the alloy’s configurational entropy (e.g. by going from a medium-entropy CoCrNi alloy to a higher-entropy CoCrFeMnNi alloy) decreases cation mobility, thickens the tribo-oxide more uniformly during the anodic off-time, and raises its mechanical integrity, so that (i) wear removal of the film falls and (ii) underlying metal dissolution is suppressed. The result is an appreciable reduction in total material degradation, dominated by a drop in the synergy term.
generation.material_initial_state: Fine-grained (≈30 µm) solution-annealed, mirror-polished CoCrNi medium-entropy alloy plates (baseline) and otherwise identically processed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy plates (intervention candidate)
generation.intervention: Add Fe and Mn to raise the configurational entropy from ~1.1 R (CoCrNi) to ~1.6 R (CoCrFeMnNi), keeping grain size, hardness (≈200 HV), surface roughness (Ra < 0.02 µm) and test geometry constant
generation.conditions: Reciprocating sliding (1 N normal load, 5 mm stroke, 1 Hz, alumina counter-ball, 25 °C) in aerated 0.6 M NaCl solution at open-circuit potential for 10 000 cycles
generation.structural_mediator: Thickness (~50–100 nm) and continuity of a Cr/Mn spinel-rich mechanically mixed tribo-oxide layer with nanocrystalline (~5 nm) grains adherent to the alloy surface
generation.mechanism: Higher configurational entropy and lattice distortion in CoCrFeMnNi slow outward cation diffusion and inward oxygen diffusion (the ‘sluggish diffusion’ effect), allowing the tribo-oxide to repassivate faster than it is mechanically removed; the denser spinel also exhibits higher hardness than the underlying metal, lowering ploughing and adhesive wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with the CoCrNi baseline, CoCrFeMnNi will show (a) ≥30 % lower total material loss after 10 000 cycles, (b) ≈40 % lower wear volume, (c) ≈25 % lower cumulative corrosion charge, and (d) ≥50 % lower calculated wear–corrosion synergy term.
generation.baseline: CoCrNi medium-entropy alloy under the same sliding/corrosion conditions
generation.boundary: Prediction holds in neutral or mildly acidic, oxidising aqueous media at temperatures ≤60 °C where Cr/Mn spinel oxides are stable. It may fail in strongly alkaline solutions, de-aerated media, or at temperatures above ~150 °C where oxide dissolution or phase transformations eliminate the protective tribo-oxide.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of reduction is uncertain (±15 %), and other factors (e.g., micro-galvanic coupling among elements, second-phase precipitation) could offset the sluggish diffusion benefit if processing history differs.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform identical tribo-corrosion tests on the CoCrNi and CoCrFeMnNi samples, continuously recording friction coefficient, open-circuit potential, and electrochemical current; measure wear tracks with 3D profilometry and quantify mass loss; analyse post-test surfaces by TEM and XPS for tribo-oxide thickness and composition.
measurements: TEM/XPS determination of tribofilm thickness and composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if CoCrFeMnNi shows (i) equal or higher total material loss than CoCrNi, OR (ii) no statistically significant (>10 %) reduction in the synergy term, OR (iii) no measurable increase in tribo-oxide thickness/continuity relative to CoCrNi under the same test conditions.
